summary: Each claim carries its writer's own signature: every member signs the claims it writes (and, in a paced background pass, those it already held) with its member key, the signatures travel beside the envelopes that carry the claims, and a peer keeps one only when it verifies with a key membership admits for that writer and names a claim of that writer. This prepares releasing envelope history; nothing reads the signatures yet

replay.detail: No replay; claims, envelopes and projections are unchanged.

schema.detail: New tables claim_member_signatures (claim, member key, signature; one row per claim and key) and claim_member_signature_pending (a verified signature whose claim has not arrived yet; dropped after 30 days if it never does). New meta keys claim_member_signature_cursor (signing pass) and claim_member_signature_pending_cursor (settling waiting signatures). No storage version change. Only an authenticated fleet peer can add waiting rows, and only with signatures that verify; the 30-day expiry is what bounds them, so a peer sending signatures for claims that never arrive costs at most a month of rows.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or fleet coordination change.

compatibility.detail: Exchanges carry an optional claim_member_signatures list beside the envelopes they send (about 200 bytes per claim). Older peers neither send nor read it; their claims get a signature once their writer runs this build and signs its own. The signed message is st3-claim-v1, fleet, writer, sequence and claim id with the writer's member key. A member keeps a peer's signature only when membership admits that key for the writer: a fleet without membership keys keeps only its members' own signatures.

downtime.detail: No startup work. After start each member signs its own retained claims in the background, 512 a page with signing outside the writer and one short write per page; on a member with three million claims of which a third are its own that is about two thousand pages.

recovery.detail: Rollback to the previous release is supported; it ignores the new tables and the exchange field.
